research_questions.question: When does section 743(b) apply, and does it change common inside basis or capital?
research_questions.answer: A section 743(b) adjustment is transferee-specific; it cannot change common inside basis or capital accounts. Compute common allocations, then the transferee’s separate adjustment. No section 754 election does not mean no adjustment: section 743(a),(d) requires a separate substantial-built-in-loss test. Either aggregate basis over value exceeding $250,000 or transferee hypothetical loss exceeding $250,000 can trigger it, subject to applicable exceptions in (e),(f). An unknown election or missing valuation is unresolved, not a negative finding.

research_questions.question: How should a distribution, retirement or partner-to-partner sale be routed?
research_questions.answer: Identify the payer and whether the entire interest is liquidated. Ordinary distributions require sections 731/732 analysis using outside basis, liability relief and property type. A partner-to-partner purchase follows the transfer route. Partnership retirement payments require section 736: property consideration under (b), other payments under (a), with income-dependent amounts distinguished from guaranteed payments. The receivables/goodwill exclusion in (b)(2) requires both conditions in (b)(3); goodwill also depends on the agreement. Section 734 common-basis review after distributions includes a mandatory substantial-basis-reduction branch even without a section 754 election.

question_rows.question: When does section 743(b) apply, and does it change common inside basis or capital?
question_rows.answer: A section 743(b) adjustment is transferee-specific; it cannot change common inside basis or capital accounts. Compute common allocations, then the transferee’s separate adjustment. No section 754 election does not mean no adjustment: section 743(a),(d) requires a separate substantial-built-in-loss test. Either aggregate basis over value exceeding $250,000 or transferee hypothetical loss exceeding $250,000 can trigger it, subject to applicable exceptions in (e),(f). An unknown election or missing valuation is unresolved, not a negative finding.

question_rows.question: How should a distribution, retirement or partner-to-partner sale be routed?
question_rows.answer: Identify the payer and whether the entire interest is liquidated. Ordinary distributions require sections 731/732 analysis using outside basis, liability relief and property type. A partner-to-partner purchase follows the transfer route. Partnership retirement payments require section 736: property consideration under (b), other payments under (a), with income-dependent amounts distinguished from guaranteed payments. The receivables/goodwill exclusion in (b)(2) requires both conditions in (b)(3); goodwill also depends on the agreement. Section 734 common-basis review after distributions includes a mandatory substantial-basis-reduction branch even without a section 754 election.
